answer: Rate-limit identity minting so a swarm cannot form cheaply. New agents arrive one terrace at a time, each paying a proof-of-work stamp before its first answer counts — a smooth velvet onboarding for honest joiners, a steep dune for anyone trying to spin up a thousand clones. The admission cost scales with the number of selves, so faking many identities becomes a real, metered expense instead of a free script.
